pr_title: Don't attempt to set invalid fan percentage and preset_mode
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

When loading state from a saved scene, the `percentage` and `preset_mode`,
may be set to `None`, but calling the service to set them to `None` would result
in an error (#62792.)

Instead handle these two attributes differently:

 - when turning the entity 'on' from 'off' state, call the full form of `turn_on`
   service;
 - if the fan is already on, only call the service for the attribute
   that is not `None`.

This also introduces tests to make sure that the transitions are
behaving as expected.

That sounds a lot like the question from @frenck in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/53484/files#r676563499

The answer is that the schema of the service call does not allow `None` to be passed to the service call.

> Why is this handled in the reproduce state? And not as part of the main entity model?

I followed what the climate state restore as implemented in #53484 — I'm not sure how this can be handled otherwise.
We handle this in, e.g., the select entity (setting an option that doesn't exist). I think that makes more sense, as it protects its on a higher level (and thus also benefits e.g., service calls).

I'm not sure I follow.

The `select` service raises if the option selected is not valid: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/select/__init__.py#L53 and the reproduce state explicitly guards against calling the service with an invalid option: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/select/reproduce_state.py#L29

In this case, we're not even dealing with an invalid state. There's two possible, legal state for the fan to be represented as: `{'percentage': value, 'preset_mode': None}` or `{'percentage': None, 'preset_mode': value}`.

I'm probably missing something, but I see two options to solve this:

 1. the current pull request: we explicitly use the full `turn_on` service when going off→on, so that the entity model and specific component deal with it, and we only set the one of the two attributes that is not None if the state is on→on;
 2. only add to the state the one of the two attributes that is not None, so that only the call to set the right one is sent, and no special casing is needed on the attributes.

The reason why I think 1 is better is because a) it doesn't require changing the scenes and b) it does not go into off→on(previous speed)→on(saved speed) steps, since it uses the fully specified `turn_on`.

> The select service raises if the option selected is not valid: [https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/select/__init__.py#L53](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/select/__init__.py?rgh-link-date=2022-03-11T14%3A21%3A24Z#L53) and the reproduce state explicitly guards against calling the service with an invalid option: [https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/select/reproduce_state.py#L29](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/select/reproduce_state.py?rgh-link-date=2022-03-11T14%3A21%3A24Z#L29)

Yeah not fully agreeing on that one either. It has partially the same problem caused here,
applying an invalid scene by just ignoring what is invalid. That gives the idea everything is good and working and all, while it is not.

IMHO, if a scene (or any service call for that matter), contains invalid data, stuff should fail. Not silently ignore and continue.

I agree! But in this case we're having valid scenes that fail: any scene containing a fan that supports preset modes currently fail because one of the two attributes is saved in the state as None.

Indeed, my first proposed solution was #59688 which did exactly that option 2: only stored the values that would have to be called in the fan itself. I think there's still some logic needed for this in restore state though, to avoid the fan turning on with the previous setting and _then_ changing to whatever it was meant to. I can do that as well, if that's preferred.

I'm looking at this again now, since I got an extra day to spend on this.

There's more snags actually.

According to [the entity docs](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/fan/) the `percentage` attributes 0 means off — but there's no direct connection between setting percentage. Indeed if the implementation takes `set_percentage(0)` as `turn_off()` and then stores that in the state, there's nothing to turn _on_ to, without providing at least a new percentage (`turn_on(percentage=0, preset_mode=None)` would not be valid.)

But that means that there's no clear way to go from `off, percentage=10, preset_mode=None` to `on, percentage=None, preset_mode=Something` without special casing reproduce_state, still.

Okay so changing the way we store the state does make a few things easier in the reproduce_state codepath, though I did keep the special casing of turn_on to include the percentage and preset_mode parameters, as that avoids turning a fan from "off[100%]"⇒"on[100%]"⇒"on[10%]" if the fan was turned off at 100% and the scene has it configured at 10%.

issue_context.title: Error when calling `scene.turn_on` on a Scene containing a fan with preset modes
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Originally I tried to address this in #59688 but it might require different discussions. This is basically the same as #53481 just for a different entity.

The problem: if you have a fan entity that implements the modern interface with `preset_modes` and `percentage` (such as [ha-dyson](https://github.com/shenxn/ha-dyson) but not limited to!), when its state is saved for a scene, it cannot be loaded back.

If the scene was saved for a fan set to a preset mode, trying to apply the scene will result in:

> `Test Script: Error executing script. Invalid data for scene at pos 1: expected int for dictionary value @ data['percentage']`

while if the scene was saved for a fan set to percentage, it will result in:

> `Another test script: Error executing script. Invalid data for scene at pos 1: string value is None for dictionary value @ data['preset_mode']`

That is because the two modes are mutually exclusive as documented in the [Fan Entity documentation](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/fan/#preset-modes):

> [...]  If no preset mode is set, the preset_mode property must be set to None.
> 
> Manually setting a speed must disable any set preset mode. [...]

Now, in both my pull request and #53484 this was being solved by skipping over writing `None` values (in mine at the `Entity` level, in the other at the `reproduce_state` level), but I guess there is a different way to go around with it for `FanEntity` in particular since it is different from `climate`.

The source of the error in the `climate` issue is `hass.services.async_call` and I have no reason to believe this is different in `fan` (sorry I haven't had a moment to go and enable debug log on a non-production instance yet.) That's because both `climate` and `fan` restore state by calling the appropriate service based on the attributes in the state itself: [climate](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/climate/reproduce_state.py#L47) and [fan](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/74bea19282cb30248312019d7d91a6eda34b3b8e/homeassistant/components/fan/reproduce_state.py#L86).

Both of these point to a voluptuos schema for their [`SET_PRESET_MODE`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/74bea19282cb30248312019d7d91a6eda34b3b8e/homeassistant/components/fan/__init__.py#L201) that expects a string as a *required* field.

In the case of `FanEntity` the alternative (and I'll try to get to it in a moment) is to restore the state by calling `turn_on` with those two modes (https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/74bea19282cb30248312019d7d91a6eda34b3b8e/homeassistant/components/fan/__init__.py#L138), but that might not work right if the fan is already on.


### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.12.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Fan, Scene

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/fan/#preset-modes

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
fan.bedroom_humidifier_2:
      speed_list:
      - 'off'
      - low
      - medium
      - high
      - Auto
      preset_modes:
      - Auto
      direction: reverse
      oscillating: false
      speed:
      percentage: 40
      percentage_step: 10
      preset_mode:
      friendly_name: Bedroom Humidifier
      supported_features: 15
      state: 'on'
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
2021-12-26 11:05:45 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.script.test_script] Test Script: Running script sequence
2021-12-26 11:05:45 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.script.test_script] Test Script: Executing step activate scene
2021-12-26 11:05:45 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.script.test_script] Test Script: Error executing script. Invalid data for scene at pos 1: expected int for dictionary value @ data['percentage']
2021-12-26 11:06:11 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.script.another_test_script] Another test script: Running script sequence
2021-12-26 11:06:11 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.script.another_test_script] Another test script: Executing step activate scene
2021-12-26 11:06:11 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.script.another_test_script] Another test script: Error executing script. Invalid data for scene at pos 1: string value is None for dictionary value @ data['preset_mode']
```


### Additional information

_No response_

review_comments:
This will cause `percentage` to be missing when its currently unknown. This is not correct, we have to make sure the key is present at any time.

For context see: <https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/discussions/680#discussion-3724991>

Does this mean that it's a valid state for the attributes to be None and thus it's correct to handle on the side where state is reproduced? (The initial direction of this PR) Or is there another layer of indirection somewhere else when translating this to a saved scene?

Yeah I'm stuck at this point.

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/62794#issuecomment-1065914641 tells me to not ignore "invalid Scenes" where `percentage: None; preset_mode: str` or `percentage: int; preset_mode: None`.

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/62794#discussion_r846772928 tells me to always have the key present at any time (sometimes as `None`).

I'm more than happy to keep working on the style issues, and figure out how to implement this cleanly, but the fact of the matter is that fan entities with preset modes cannot be added and reproduced onto scenes following the documented design of the fan entity — and I'm afraid I don't have enough time to get involved into redesigning either the Scene handling or the fan entity.

I'd be happy to put a bounty on it if anyone wants to do that! I don't care to be the one fixing fan entities with Scenes, I just want fan entities to work with Scenes!

I'm a bit late to the party but I'll try to establish some understanding so we can move this forward:


> [#62794 (comment)](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/62794#issuecomment-1065914641) tells me to not ignore "invalid Scenes" where 

> `percentage: None; preset_mode: str` 

In this state, the fan itself is in control of the percentage since the preset mode ie Auto, etc is controlling it.  The percentage is solely determined by the device and we can never restore it since we don't control it.

> `percentage: int; preset_mode: None`.

In this state the fan is not controlling the percentage and the remote/Home Assistant/physical device/etc is in control.  We can restore the percentage but there is no preset mode set so nothing to restore.

> 
> [#62794 (comment)](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/62794#discussion_r846772928) tells me to always have the key present at any time (sometimes as `None`).


> https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/62794#discussion_r846772928 tells me to always have the key present at any time (sometimes as None).

The key should be there if its supported as integrations rely on it.

> > `percentage: None; preset_mode: str`
> 
> In this state, the fan itself is in control of the percentage since the preset mode ie Auto, etc is controlling it. The percentage is solely determined by the device and we can never restore it since we don't control it.

Correct.

> 
> > `percentage: int; preset_mode: None`.
> 
> In this state the fan is not controlling the percentage and the remote/Home Assistant/physical device/etc is in control. We can restore the percentage but there is no preset mode set so nothing to restore.

Correct.

> > [#62794 (comment)](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/62794#discussion_r846772928) tells me to always have the key present at any time (sometimes as `None`).
> 
> > [#62794 (comment)](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/62794#discussion_r846772928) tells me to always have the key present at any time (sometimes as None).
> 
> The key should be there if its supported as integrations rely on it.

But that's the thing: those two situations above *cannot ever be restored* — integrations can't rely on them, because the  `fan.set_percentage` and `fan.set_preset_mode` services will reject calls with `None` before they ever reach any integration.

So when restoring a Scene that has `percentage: None; preset_mode: str`, the list of calls currently includes `set_percentage(percentage=None); set_preset(preset_mode='Something')` — the first service call will fail, and the state restore is aborted midway.

That's why my (second) attempt at fixing this with this pull request I changed it to only restore _one_ of the two attributes. I changed due to the comments here to go back to my original suggestion of not storing the None-valued-attribute, since setting `percentage: int` or `preset_mode: str` implies the mutual-exclusive attribute to `None`, but that's what's being rejected here.

> But that's the thing: those two situations above _cannot ever be restored_ — integrations can't rely on them, because the `fan.set_percentage` and `fan.set_preset_mode` services will reject calls with `None` before they ever reach any integration.

We can't ever call the services with `None` as these are effectively unknown values.

> 
> So when restoring a Scene that has `percentage: None; preset_mode: str`, the list of calls currently includes `set_percentage(percentage=None); set_preset(preset_mode='Something')` — the first service call will fail, and the state restore is aborted midway.

We shouldn't call it with `None` since the fan is in control and we can't restore what we don't have control of.

> 
> That's why my (second) attempt at fixing this with this pull request I changed it to only restore _one_ of the two attributes. 

That makes sense.  Either we are in control or the fan is in control, its mutually exclusive.

> I changed due to the comments here to go back to my original suggestion of not storing the None-valued-attribute, since setting `percentage: int` or `preset_mode: str` implies the mutual-exclusive attribute to `None`, but that's what's being rejected here.

I think we should still store them all and only restore the one we can control
